llm.summary: The rate-relief mechanism that powered yesterday's AI bounce has reversed in a single session: crude is at a five-month high on Houthi strikes on Saudi energy/airport sites and deadlocked US-Iran talks, the 10-year is above 5.1%, gold is down a third straight day, and a Reuters poll now has all 100 economists expecting a December Fed hike after an October skip. Risk is being repriced not by growth fear but by the cost of money. On top of that, the AI balance-sheet crack widened — a Korean data-center IPO broke 30% below issue, dragging the whole data-center complex, while HSBC's CEO publicly warned that not every data center is a good bet, even as Anthropic and Nscale discuss a second multibillion (reported ~$45bn) cloud deal. The income statement still prints: NOC beat and raised with a swelling backlog, GE Aerospace raised on a 49% order surge, EFX gapped +10.6%, SYF reported record purchase volume with strong credit. The real-economy casualty is housing — pending sales at a 25-year low, starts -5.9%, builder sentiment at 2012 lows — and it is the single loudest signal in public attention (72, +43% vs 28d) while being flagged as not priced. Flows confirm the rotation rather than a liquidation: Energy 84, Health Care 60, Staples 51 against Industrials -40, Comm Services -29, Real Estate -50, with Value beating Growth by 25 points. For the book, the live item is Salesforce paying a 58% premium in stock for Braze and getting a chilly reception — a capital-discipline question inside a holding whose thesis was improving FCF and a cheap-versus-history multiple. Netflix, RTX, ISRG, COF and PM print into this tape.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: risk-off tilt inside a rotation, not a crash. Oil round-tripping to a five-month high while the 10-year sits above 5.1% removes the only support yesterday's AI bounce had, and a unanimous December-hike expectation means equity multiples have no discount-rate help into year-end. The dispersion trade sharpens: long the AI income statement (NOC/GE/RTX backlogs, EFX, memory and on-device inference) and short the AI balance sheet (neoclouds, data-center IPOs, leveraged compute intermediaries). The Korean data-center IPO breaking 30% is a primary-market verdict and primary markets lead sell-side sentiment; Nscale/Anthropic's $45bn headline is the counter-signal and the two cannot both be right. Netflix tonight is the highest-variance single event with Communication Services flows deteriorating at -29 rotation. Energy, Health Care and Staples keep absorbing the flow.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the regime distribution has decisively fattened its inflationary tails — Reflation 31.8 (+14.4) and Stagflation 29.0 (+10.3) versus Goldilocks 20.5 (-10.3). Oil-led inflation plus an AI capex cycle that is itself an inflation input means the Fed tightens into the buildout rather than financing it. That combination is lethal for rate-sensitive real economy assets (housing starts, builders, REITs at -50 rotation, small caps) and supportive for anything with contracted cash flow, pricing power or a backlog: defense primes, aerospace aftermarket, regulated power, copper, energy. Copper outperforming gold this year — and investors arguing the rally survives an AI correction — is the tell that the electrification bid is physical demand, not a monetary trade. Gold's three-day slide against a CIBC forecast cut is a real-rate problem, not a thesis break; fiscal debasement keeps a floor near $4,000. The consumer stays bifurcated: SYF record volume and strong credit at one end, paycheck-to-paycheck pessimism and a frozen housing market at the other.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: three structural migrations are compounding. First, the compute moat moves from silicon to software-plus-power — Amazon's TorchNeuron letting 85% of AI developers run code on Trainium is the second week running of a credible assault on CUDA switching costs, and even partial success compresses the terminal margin embedded in the whole semiconductor complex. Second, AI leaves the data center: Nvidia's German industrial-AI tie-up, stakes in Agile Robots, local agents on RTX Spark laptops, and AMD's push on real-time control for physical AI decouple adoption from hyperscaler capex and re-rate the edge-device, sensing and automation supply chain. Third, electricity becomes the scarce industrial good of the decade — Meta funding seven gas plants for a single campus, Indiana eyeing 6GW of nuclear, the UK paying record grid-balancing sums — so siting follows electrons and whoever owns ratebase, turbines, pipelines or uprated nuclear gets paid regardless of which model wins. Underneath all of it, a decade-long housing transaction freeze permanently redirects household spending from shelter formation toward services, experiences, health and cost-removal.

short_term: Households are abandoning the home purchase decision outright rather than waiting — pending sales at a 25-year low and 'housing market crash' among top rising queries means the behaviour is capitulation, not deferral; rent and renovation spend absorbs what mortgages would have.

Energy cost is back as a visible household line item: oil at five-month highs, European wholesale gas above €90, and 'electricity bill assistance' queries rising — this crowds out discretionary spend in Q4 and supports value retail over aspiration retail.

Investors are paying for backlogs and cash flow rather than narratives: NOC +6.6% on a raise, EFX gapping +10.6%, GE raising on a 49% order surge, while a data-center IPO breaks 30% and Salesforce gets punished for a 58% acquisition premium.

Risk capital is discriminating within AI for the first time — HSBC's CEO saying not every data center is a good bet, HSBC reviewing its Palantir position in a $9bn fund, Korean and Hong Kong IPOs pricing weak — that is selective, not wholesale, de-risking.

Consumers still spend on identity and entertainment even while squeezed: Hasbro raising guidance on $600m of Magic: The Gathering, Best Buy building a gaming hub into Zelda/GTA VI, festive travel ranking top-three in spending surveys.
Credit behaviour has not broken: SYF reports record purchase volume with strong credit, which means the squeeze is currently showing up as trade-down and deferral rather than delinquency.
long_term: Shelter is being reclassified from a wealth-building asset to a consumption expense for a growing cohort of households, structurally shrinking home-equity-funded spending and enlarging the renter services, storage and small-format retail economy.

Energy security is being nationalised as a consumer and sovereign need, not just a corporate one — Vietnam diversifying LNG supply, Indonesia's $3.8tn pivot, the EU's Arctic strategy for raw materials and routes — which makes long-dated supply contracts and grid assets politically protected cash flows.

People increasingly buy cost removal and verified identity rather than new capability: agentic software, credit and identity data, and automation of labour are where corporate wallets migrate as wage growth stagnates against 3%+ inflation.

Compute is becoming a personal utility — local agents on laptops, Nvidia RTX Spark, 85% of developers able to target alternative silicon — shifting value from centralized inference rent toward devices, on-prem and the tools layer.

Status and connection are migrating into cheap, repeatable digital goods (trading-card ecosystems, gaming, short-form commerce via TikTok Shop and Temu) as big-ticket status purchases — homes, new vehicles — become unattainable for the median household.

Health is being purchased as continuous monitoring rather than episodic treatment, which privileges sensors, surgical robotics and chronic-care devices over acute hospital spend as the population ages into a higher-rate, lower-wealth-growth environment.
